heading: Frequently asked questions
subheading: Quick answers to common questions about how Fleent works, pricing, and privacy.

items.question: Is Fleent only for people with ADHD?
items.answer: Not at all. Fleent is for anyone who struggles to start - whether you have ADHD, anxiety, or just find yourself staring at your to-do list, doing nothing. If getting started is hard, Fleent is for you.

items.question: Why only 3 tasks?
items.answer: Because more than 3 is where overwhelm starts. Fleent keeps your focus narrow on purpose - when one task is done, another can join. Less scrolling, more doing.

items.question: How does the AI breakdown work?
items.answer: Type in any task and Fleent's AI splits it into the smallest possible physical steps. Instead of "write report," you get "open a blank doc, write one sentence." Steps you can actually start.

items.question: Is my data private?
items.answer: Yes. Your tasks are yours. We don't sell your data or share it with third parties.

items.question: Is Fleent free?
items.answer: Most of Fleent is completely free - your 3-task dashboard, focus timer, and pet are all included at no cost. AI-powered features like task breakdowns are part of our paid plan, for when you're ready to let Fleent do the heavy thinking for you.

items.question: What is the pet timer?
items.answer: That's Fleent - your focus buddy. They start cold and sad when you haven't begun, and warm up as you work. When the flame appears, you're in flow. It's a small thing that makes a big difference.

items.question: Does it work on mobile?
items.answer: Yes - Fleent runs right in your browser on desktop and mobile, so you can pick up your top 3 wherever you are.

items.question: What if I can't finish a task in one session?
items.answer: No guilt here. Fleent tracks the days you showed up and started - not whether you finished. Progress is progress.

items.question: What if I can't even start the "easy" step?
items.answer: Hit the AI breakdown again and go smaller. There's no floor on how tiny a step can be. "Open the document" is a valid step. So is "find my charger." Start there.
